title: Leave a broken order out of the nightly import, whole

blocks.text: Every night a partner shop's orders are imported in one transaction. Now and then the partner sends a line the database refuses: a missing SKU, or one longer than twelve characters. The warehouse has started finding orders in its pick lists that have some of their lines but not all, and the partner is asking why a few orders never arrive at all.

`importAll(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/OrderImport.java` already runs the night in one transaction and commits once. Finish `importOne(...)`, which writes one order with `insertOrder` and `insertLine` and says whether the order made it into the import.
When you're done, an order the database refuses any part of is left out entirely, and every other order of the night is imported with all its lines. About eight lines.
The tests import into an in-memory H2 database and check what a second connection sees after the commit.

cases.says: a night without a refused row imports every order with all its lines
an order with a refused line leaves none of its lines in the database
orders imported before a refused one are still committed
an order with a refused line leaves no order row behind either

origin.section: A Failed Statement Undoes Only Itself; a Savepoint Undoes the Group

concepts: rollback(savepoint) undoes everything after the savepoint and keeps the transaction open, so a savepoint at the start of each group of statements drops a bad group whole.
On H2 a failed statement undoes only itself: the transaction stays open, and a later commit keeps the statements before it.
